      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag. (#1431): the SDK pin must be an EXACT
          # 3.47.x patch (no wildcard) — a floating patch re-resolves a new
          # engine build and moves the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the
          # size gates track.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do

# recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag. (#1431): the SDK pin must be an EXACT
          # 3.47.x patch (no wildcard) — a floating patch re-resolves a new
          # engine build and moves the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the
          # size gates track.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -Eq "flutter-version: '3\.47\.[0-9]+'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity + #1431 exact-patch rule, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

Good — `type a number: ` is the picker prompt, re-rendered per menu. Now I have everything for the RED tests. Writing them into the reg test file, extending the "a sanctioned mid-session write survives the next persist (gh-1572 rework)" group with four tests:

1. `the real ttsr toggle fires the re-sync hook` (count pin)
2. `the real mcp edit fires the re-sync hook` (count pin)
3. `the ttsr toggle survives the next persist (flow re-sync)` (end-to-end)
4. `the mcp edit survives the next persist (flow re-sync)` (end-to-end)

Actually — to keep it tight, 2 tests might suffice: end-to-end ones inherently pin the hook (they fail without it). But the count pins give precise failure diagnostics and match the reviewer's ask ("add the two flows to the reg group"). I'll write: ttsr end-to-end (includes implicit hook dependence) + mcp end-to-end + a combined hook-count test asserting both flows fire exactly once. Three tests.

Driver details:
- helper `waitForIo(predicate)` polling `io.out` with timeout.
- helper `renderCount(io, n)` = wait until 'type a number:' occurs n times.

TTSR script (from settings_flow_test AC2):
- seed: model + ttsr block (one disabled rule 'no-secrets' + memory? skip memory).
- boot cli (with hook counter that re-syncs snapshot like the real bin).
- `final flow = cli.startTtsrRulesFlow();`
- wait 1 render; sendLine('1') (the rule) → rule submenu; wait 2 renders; sendLine('1') (toggle) → 'ttsr saved → ...' appears; wait 3 renders (menu re-rendered); sendLine('3') (done — the menu in reg seed has 1 rule + add + done = 3 options, so done = 3! The settings test had 2 rules → done was 4. My seed has 1 rule → menu = [rule, add, done] → done='3'). Then `await flow`.
- assert hook fired (resyncs == 1) and disk shows enabled: true.
- then persistShapedSave(snapshot) where snapshot re-synced via hook (like the real bin wiring), then reload → the rule stays enabled (end-to-end test).

Wait — the end-to-end test: snapshot var, hook closure re-syncs it. After the flow, `persistShapedSave(snapshot)` → without the hook the snapshot is stale (enabled: false) → the save re-renders the stale ttsr → the toggle is lost → RED. With the hook → green.

MCP script (from settings_flow_mcp_test AC2):
- seed: model + mcp block (one stdio server 'fs') — done option = [server fs, add, done] → done = '3'.
- `final flow = cli.startMcpServersFlow();`
- wait 1 render; sendLine('1') (fs) → submenu (1=edit? check `_mcpServerAction` submenu: 'edit'/'delete'/'back'?); wait 2; sendLine('1') (edit); command prompt: sendLine('node2'); args: sendLine('srv.js'); env prompt: hmm — the stdio edit prompts command, args, env. For a server seeded WITHOUT env, the env prompt may be skipped or asked with keep-on-empty. In the AC2 test the server had env FOO=bar and it prompted 'BAZ=qux'. For minimal prompting: args prompt accepts empty (keeps), env prompt accepts empty (keeps). The prompts: "command (empty keeps 'npx'):" → sendLine('node2'); "args (empty keeps ...)": → sendLine(''); "env (empty keeps ...)": → sendLine(''). Then 'mcp saved → ...'.
- then done '3', await flow; assert hook count and persistence.

Let me check the edit prompt sequence + submenu numbering in `_mcpServerAction`/`_promptMcpServerBody`.

2. `the real mcp edit fires the re-sync hook` (count pin)
3. `the ttsr toggle survives the next persist (flow re-sync)` (end-to-end)
4. `the mcp edit survives the next persist (flow re-sync)` (end-to-end)

Actually — to keep it tight, 2 tests might suffice: end-to-end ones inherently pin the hook (they fail without it). But the count pins give precise failure diagnostics and match the reviewer's ask ("add the two flows to the reg group"). I'll write: ttsr end-to-end (includes implicit hook dependence) + mcp end-to-end + a combined hook-count test asserting both flows fire exactly once. Three tests.

Driver details:
- helper `waitForIo(predicate)` polling `io.out` with timeout.
- helper `renderCount(io, n)` = wait until 'type a number:' occurs n times.

TTSR script (from settings_flow_test AC2):
- seed: model + ttsr block (one disabled rule 'no-secrets' + memory? skip memory).
- boot cli (with hook counter that re-syncs snapshot like the real bin).
- `final flow = cli.startTtsrRulesFlow();`
- wait 1 render; sendLine('1') (the rule) → rule submenu; wait 2 renders; sendLine('1') (toggle) → 'ttsr saved → ...' appears; wait 3 renders (menu re-rendered); sendLine('3') (done — the menu in reg seed has 1 rule + add + done = 3 options, so done = 3! The settings test had 2 rules → done was 4. My seed has 1 rule → menu = [rule, add, done] → done='3'). Then `await flow`.
- assert hook fired (resyncs == 1) and disk shows enabled: true.
- then persistShapedSave(snapshot) where snapshot re-synced via hook (like the real bin wiring), then reload → the rule stays enabled (end-to-end test).

Wait — the end-to-end test: snapshot var, hook closure re-syncs it. After the flow, `persistShapedSave(snapshot)` → without the hook the snapshot is stale (enabled: false) → the save re-renders the stale ttsr → the toggle is lost → RED. With the hook → green.

MCP script (from settings_flow_mcp_test AC2):

- `final flow = cli.startMcpServersFlow();`

4:title: "flutter_agent_harness gh-1572 rework contract (pr-1587): `AgentCliConfig.onUserConfigFileChanged` (wired in bin/fah_runapp.dart to `saved = loadCliConfig(home)`, ConfigException-guarded) fires after EVERY sanctioned direct write to the USER ~/.fah/config.yaml — `_upsertConfigYaml` (global scope only), `_clearContextCap`, `_dropAutoUpdateKey`, `_removeCapabilityYaml` (fire helper `_notifyUserConfigFileChanged` in settings_flow_config_sync.dart). persistConfig's base is the mutable boot `saved`, so any NEW settings flow that writes the user config directly MUST fire the hook or the next persist resurrects the pre-write values. Project-scope writes don't fire it (snapshot tracks the user file only). `validateAgentSection` (config_service.dart) must know every key the `agent:` emitter renders (contextWindowCap/mode/misuseBreaker/stuckTool — pinned by the \"everything the emitter renders passes the strict mirror validator\" test); `_diskPreservedSections` must list every top-level key with no typed renderer (providersQueue was the last gap). Context-cap flow now lives in settings_flow_context_cap.dart (clear = key-only removeYamlPath, not the whole block)."

And then it timed out at line 569 — which is `waitRenders(io, 2)` after sending '1'. So sendLine('1') didn't advance the flow. Why? The picker prompt appeared... The `render` counting: 'type a number:' appeared ONCE. waitRenders(io, 1) passed. Then `io.sendLine('1')` → the line goes to `_lines` controller. But the picker's `_promptLine` may have started listening AFTER... no — the prompt printed before my sendLine (waitRenders(io,1) succeeded after the prompt was printed). Unless the FIRST 'type a number:' was printed during waitRenders(1) and my sendLine raced BEFORE `_promptLine` subscribed to io.lines. `_promptLine` prints 'type a number: ' THEN awaits the line — there's an await gap between print and listen. My waitRenders polls every 10ms — it could observe the prompt before the listener attached, send '1' into the broadcast controller with no listener → line dropped → hang. The settings_flow_test uses `render(n)` (same race!) — but they also run `cli.run()` concurrently which may prime things... Actually StreamController here is a plain broadcast? `final _lines = StreamController<String>();` — NOT broadcast — a single-listener controller buffers events until listened! So an early sendLine would be buffered and delivered once `_promptLine` listens. That's not the issue then...

Wait — is the FIRST sendLine consumed by something else? Hmm: `bootCli` never runs `cli.run()`. In settings_flow_test, `cli.run()` is active. Maybe `_promptLine` (line 50ish) uses `_pendingPromptAnswer` mechanism wired through the run loop?! Look: `_promptLine` at provider_flow_helpers.dart:~50: it creates a `pending` Completer, listens to io.interrupts... and the actual line reading — maybe via `io.lines` with a subscription stored on the CLI (`_attachLineFeed`?) that only exists when run() is active. The `_pendingPromptAnswer` field suggests the run loop feeds prompts: run() listens to io.lines and completes `_pendingPromptAnswer`. Without run(), nobody completes the pending → hang with the menu rendered. That matches the observed state: menu printed, prompt printed, sendLine buffered but never consumed.

... drive ...

```

4:title: "flutter_agent_harness gh-1572 rework contract (pr-1587): `AgentCliConfig.onUserConfigFileChanged` (wired in bin/fah_runapp.dart to `saved = loadCliConfig(home)`, ConfigException-guarded) fires after EVERY sanctioned direct write to the USER ~/.fah/config.yaml — `_upsertConfigYaml` (global scope only), `_clearContextCap`, `_dropAutoUpdateKey`, `_removeCapabilityYaml` (fire helper `_notifyUserConfigFileChanged` in settings_flow_config_sync.dart). persistConfig's base is the mutable boot `saved`, so any NEW settings flow that writes the user config directly MUST fire the hook or the next persist resurrects the pre-write values. Project-scope writes don't fire it (snapshot tracks the user file only). `validateAgentSection` (config_service.dart) must know every key the `agent:` emitter renders (contextWindowCap/mode/misuseBreaker/stuckTool — pinned by the \"everything the emitter renders passes the strict mirror validator\" test); `_diskPreservedSections` must list every top-level key with no typed renderer (providersQueue was the last gap). Context-cap flow now lives in settings_flow_context_cap.dart (clear = key-only removeYamlPath, not the whole block)."

4:title: "flutter_agent_harness gh-1572 rework contract (pr-1587): `AgentCliConfig.onUserConfigFileChanged` (wired in bin/fah_runapp.dart to `saved = loadCliConfig(home)`, ConfigException-guarded) fires after EVERY sanctioned direct write to the USER ~/.fah/config.yaml — `_upsertConfigYaml` (global scope only), `_clearContextCap`, `_dropAutoUpdateKey`, `_removeCapabilityYaml` (fire helper `_notifyUserConfigFileChanged` in settings_flow_config_sync.dart). persistConfig's base is the mutable boot `saved`, so any NEW settings flow that writes the user config directly MUST fire the hook or the next persist resurrects the pre-write values. Project-scope writes don't fire it (snapshot tracks the user file only). `validateAgentSection` (config_service.dart) must know every key the `agent:` emitter renders (contextWindowCap/mode/misuseBreaker/stuckTool — pinned by the \"everything the emitter renders passes the strict mirror validator\" test); `_diskPreservedSections` must list every top-level key with no typed renderer (providersQueue was the last gap). Context-cap flow now lives in settings_flow_context_cap.dart (clear = key-only removeYamlPath, not the whole block)."
